title: Side Chapter · Void Machines
subtitle: What the void materials from Hoanna make

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:ultra_heat_generator}
entries.summary: The longer it burns, the hotter and stronger
items: essentialcraft5:ultra_heat_generator

blocks.text: Void stone keeps the radiance out. Thirty fathoms deeper and there would be enough to wall the whole city. They keep pressing us from above. We started digging too late.
blocks.by: Carved in a mine shaft, Hoanna

blocks.text: Goal (optional): upgrade the [[generators/heat_generator|Heat Generator]] into an {item:essentialcraft5:ultra_heat_generator}. It still burns fuel, but it also has a heat value that only ever rises. The longer it burns, the hotter it gets and the more it makes, and once it is hot, one of them outdoes several ordinary generators.
Rare materials for this chapter

Of the void materials you bring back from Hoanna, the two rarest come from a craft the people of Hoanna only learned near the end. All six things in this chapter need a {item:essentialcraft5:void_core} from the chests of Hoanna's ruins in Chapter 16, and all but the Building Wand need an {item:essentialcraft5:void_mru_reactor} as well. A chest gives about 0.2 of each on average ([[hoanna/relics]]). {item:essentialcraft5:void_plating} is easy to come by, since you can press it from Void Stone on the Magician Table ([[hoanna/void_plating]]).

rows: Matter of Eternity, World Interacting Device
Matter of Eternity, World Interacting Device

blocks.text: Building all six takes 8 cores and 7 reactors, or roughly 40 chests. The later main chapters, [[demons]], [[hologram]], [[inquisitorium]] and [[computer]], use roughly another 15 cores and 12 reactors, and [[gear/void_armor]] takes 8 cores and 5 reactors more. All three together come to about 155 chests, so set the main-line share aside first and then build what you want most.

blocks.title: Which one first
blocks.text: If your cores only stretch to one generator and you have a steady supply of logs, such as a tree farm, pick the [[void_machines/ultra_natural_furnace]]. It makes {cfg:machines.ultra_natural_furnace.mru_log} MRU a tick the moment a log goes in. If you would rather leave it running and let it grow, pick the Ultra Heat Generator, which reaches 82 a tick after 12 minutes of warm-up, a little over 100 after an hour and about 180 after ten hours.
A {item:essentialcraft5:matter_of_eternity} is made on the Magician Table from one Nether Star and 4 Large MRU Chunks ([[storage/soul_storage]]).
Nether Stars can also be condensed in a {item:essentialcraft5:ley_condenser} ([[ley/condensing]]), so you don't have to fight a Wither for each one.
Prepare

4 {item:essentialcraft5:void_plating}s, 2 {item:essentialcraft5:void_mru_reactor}s and 2 {item:essentialcraft5:void_core}s around a Heat Generator in the middle. Bring 4 buckets of lava as well, plus about 72 coal for the warm-up, or 8 coal blocks or 6 lava buckets in its place.

Heat sources are placed and counted exactly as for the Heat Generator, two blocks out to the north, south, east and west, but here they only set how fast it heats up and add nothing to the output. Lava on all four sides heats it fastest, and a single side of air stops the heating completely.
How to do it

items: Choose the spot before you place it. Breaking it resets the heat to zero, so moving it means warming up from scratch.
Following the picture, place lava two blocks out on each of the four sides.
Link the machines that use MRU to it with [[crafting/bound_gem|Bound Gems]], so the MRU it makes has somewhere to go.
Put fuel in the left slot, which only takes things that burn. It starts burning and heating up right away.
Let it warm up. With lava on all four sides and coal as fuel, it reaches 10,000°C in about 12 minutes and then makes 82 MRU per tick.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: The number on the "Heat" line in its screen keeps climbing, and the output grows with it.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: The first two and a half minutes eat fuel fast, about a piece of coal every two seconds, and one stack of 64 gets it to about 1,000°C, so keep it topped up. Something has to draw its MRU during the warm-up as well. With nothing attached it fills up within a few minutes, and once full it stops lighting new fuel and the heat stops rising.
Heat and output

rows: <w>25–49 ticks</w>, more as it gets hotter

blocks.text: Above 1,000°C a piece of coal lasts the full 80 seconds. Poorer heat sources warm it up far more slowly. Reaching 1,000°C takes about 167 coal with netherrack on all four sides, and about 841 with plain stone.
Fine print

items: Each tick it burns, the heat rises by "product of the four factors × heating rate". Below 1,000°C the rate climbs slowly from 0.1 to 1, between 1,000 and 10,000°C it stays at 1, and above that it is 9,990 ÷ heat, so the hotter it gets, the slower it climbs.
Output depends only on the heat. Once it is hot you can take the lava away and it keeps producing at its current heat. It just stops heating up.

It holds {cfg:machines.ultra_heat_generator.max_mru} MRU. When full it stops lighting new fuel, but the piece already burning goes on burning and heating. The heat never drops, and it rises again once machines draw from it.
A redstone signal stops the whole machine, and both the heat and the burn progress are kept.
Each fuel item it lights adds a piece of {item:essentialcraft5:magical_slag} to the right slot, and a lava bucket leaves an empty bucket behind. Hoppers can pull out both.

items.text: There is no heat limit. It keeps heating up for as long as it burns.

When placed it rolls a random balance between 0 and 2 and keeps it from then on. Below 1 leans {balance:frozen} and above 1 leans {balance:chaos} (see [[start/glossary]]). Breaking and replacing it rerolls the balance but also resets the heat, so check the balance before you start warming it up.
The MRU it makes always has a balance of {cfg:machines.ultra_heat_generator.balance} (see [[start/glossary]]).

blocks.text: Further reading: heat source factors in [[generators/heat_generator]]; getting MRU into machines in [[crafting/bound_gem]].
The original research book made a point of adding "There is no heat limit too!" and said that the hotter it gets, the less fuel it burns.

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:ultra_natural_furnace}
entries.summary: Burns flowers, leaves, grass and logs
items: essentialcraft5:ultra_natural_furnace

blocks.text: Goal (optional): upgrade the [[generators/natural_furnace|Natural Furnace]] into an {item:essentialcraft5:ultra_natural_furnace}. It burns flowers, leaves, grass and logs instead, makes far more per tick than the regular one, and gets the most out of logs.
Prepare

It takes the same 4 {item:essentialcraft5:void_plating}s, 2 {item:essentialcraft5:void_mru_reactor}s and 2 {item:essentialcraft5:void_core}s as the Ultra Heat Generator, with a Natural Furnace in the middle instead. Chop a few stacks of logs to burn as well.
How to do it

items: Place it, then link your MRU-using machines to it with [[crafting/bound_gem|Bound Gems]] before anything else.
Put logs, leaves, flowers or grass into its only slot, up to a full stack of 64.
It lights one item at a time and burns it for a set time depending on its kind, making a fixed amount of MRU per tick. Nothing is left afterwards.
A {item:minecraft:hopper} or pipe can feed it from any side, though it only accepts the kinds listed below, so a steady line of logs keeps it going.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: Once something burnable is in, the flame lights up and its screen shows the output per tick.
What it burns

cells: Grass, ferns (tall ones too) and tall flowers
Logs (stripped logs and wood blocks too)

blocks.text: Total per item = ticks it burns × MRU per tick

A log burns for {cfg:machines.ultra_natural_furnace.ticks_log} ticks at {cfg:machines.ultra_natural_furnace.mru_log} MRU per tick, far more in total than anything else, so chopping trees is the best way to fuel it.
Sunflowers, lilacs, rose bushes, peonies and the other tall flowers count as grass. Saplings, Nether stems, bamboo and dead bushes don't go in at all.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: It only holds {cfg:machines.ultra_natural_furnace.max_mru} MRU and fills up within seconds on logs. Once it is full, the rest of whatever is burning goes to waste. If your machines draw slowly, link a [[storage/charging_chamber]] too and put a big soul storage item in it, so the extra MRU is saved for the things you carry.
Fine print

items: Compared with the regular Natural Furnace, small flowers and grass give more here, but tall flowers count as grass and give less than they would in the regular one.
When full it stops lighting new items, but the one already burning finishes.
A redstone signal stops it, and the burn progress is kept.
Hoppers and pipes can't pull anything out of its slot.

items.text: When placed it rolls a random balance between 0 and 2, shown in its screen. If you don't like the number, break it and place it again (see [[start/glossary]]).
The MRU it makes always has a balance of {cfg:machines.ultra_natural_furnace.balance} (see [[start/glossary]]).

blocks.text: Further reading: the regular version in [[generators/natural_furnace]]; storing MRU in items you carry in [[storage/soul_storage]].

In the original mod it went looking for flowers, grass, leaves and logs within a dozen or so blocks and set them alight by itself, and it even replanted saplings that fell nearby. Now it only burns what you put in its slot and leaves the woods around it alone.

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:magical_furnace}
items: essentialcraft5:magical_furnace
entries.summary: Toss items on top; results land on the corners

blocks.text: Goal (optional): build a Magical Furnace. Toss logs, sand, raw ores or anything else a furnace takes onto it, and it finishes one item every {cfg:machines.magical_furnace.ticks_required|sec}, sometimes with an extra result.
Prepare

items: The machine itself takes a {item:essentialcraft5:magical_screen}, an {item:essentialcraft5:void_mru_reactor}, a {item:essentialcraft5:world_interactor}, 2 {item:essentialcraft5:magic_fortified_plating}s, a {item:essentialcraft5:void_core}, 2 {item:essentialcraft5:void_plating}s and 1 {item:essentialcraft5:matter_of_eternity}. The recipe is below.
Cores and reactors come from [[hoanna/relics]], the Matter of Eternity takes a Nether Star ([[storage/soul_storage]]), and the other parts are in [[crafting/magician_crafts]].
29 {item:essentialcraft5:void_stone} in any colors ([[hoanna/void_stone]]).
4 ordinary {item:essentialcraft5:heat_generator}s ([[generators/heat_generator]]). Ultra Heat Generators won't do.
A {item:essentialcraft5:bound_gem} linked to an MRU source ([[crafting/bound_gem]]).

blocks.text: Layout

Lay a 5×5 floor of Void Stone and put the furnace on the middle block. Put a Void Stone on each corner of the furnace's layer and a Heat Generator on each corner of the layer above. The generators are only stands here and need no fuel.
How to do it

items: Right-click the furnace and put the bound gem in its only slot to power it. If the structure is wrong, hover over the status bar in its screen to see which block is off.
Stand next to it and toss what you want smelted onto the furnace. A whole stack at once is fine.
Each finished item drops its result on top of the south-east Heat Generator, and a piece of {item:essentialcraft5:magical_slag} on the north-east one.
Come back now and then to pick up what has landed on the corners.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: The status in its screen reads "Smelting", the tossed stack shrinks, and results turn up on the south-east corner with slag on the north-east one.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: Once 8 or more piles of dropped items lie on one corner, it stops and the status reads "Output corners are full" until you clear them. Items on the ground despawn after a while, so after tossing a whole chest's worth on it, stay nearby.
Numbers

rows: 1 per item on the north-east corner; {cfg:machines.magical_furnace.double_slag_chance|pct} chance of 1 more on the south-west corner

blocks.title: Which furnace?
blocks.text: For ores and raw ores alone, the {item:essentialcraft5:magmatic_smeltery} is the better deal ([[magmatic/smeltery]]). The Magical Furnace smelts anything, needs no lava and works quickly. The {item:essentialcraft5:magic_magmatic_furnace} has a similar name but is actually a tier of the Magmatic Furnace ([[magmatic/furnace_upgrades]]).
Fine print

items: If MRU runs out halfway, the progress pauses and carries on once MRU is back, so nothing is wasted. Only a different kind of item, an empty top or a missing structure block starts it over.
A redstone signal stops it and keeps the progress.
Results merge into a matching pile nearby first, so a corner usually holds only one or two piles.

To collect automatically, place a [[logistics/magical_hopper]] nearby with a filter that only lets the results and slag through ([[logistics/filters]]). Without a filter it also carries off the items you tossed on top to be smelted.
Wet Sponges and dusts never give an extra result, though slag comes out as usual, so re-wetting, or grinding and smelting again, can't make items out of nothing.
It leaves alone drops meant for another player and display items.

blocks.text: The original research book subtitled it "Not an Infernal one". Another magic mod of the time had a big furnace that swallowed dropped items too, and the line most likely sets the two apart.

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:magical_teleporter}
items: essentialcraft5:magical_teleporter
entries.summary: Stand on it to reach the block a gem is bound to

blocks.text: Goal (optional): build a Magical Teleporter. Stand on it until it is charged and you are sent to the top of the block a bound gem points at, however far away it is in the same world.
It crosses dimensions too, so the Overworld, the Nether, the End and Hoanna are each one trip from the others.
Teleporting into Hoanna, though, needs matrix rank {cfg:general.matrix_rank.gates.hoanna_portal}; below that, the teleporter won't send you. Leaving Hoanna never checks your rank.
Prepare

items: The machine itself uses the Magical Furnace recipe, except that the sides become {item:essentialcraft5:magic_plate}s, and pale, mithriline or demonic plates work there too. It needs a {item:essentialcraft5:matter_of_eternity} as well.
36 {item:essentialcraft5:void_stone} and 4 {item:essentialcraft5:magic_plating}, any colors ([[hoanna/void_stone]], [[alloys/plating]]).
Two {item:essentialcraft5:bound_gem}s, one linked to an MRU source and one bound to the destination block ([[crafting/bound_gem]]).

blocks.text: Layout
The teleporter's layer is 5×5. The four blocks two steps east, south, west and north of it are Magic Plating, and everything else is Void Stone.

On each of the two layers above, put two Void Stones on every side so they form four pairs of pillars. The corners and the middle stay empty, leaving two blocks of room above the teleporter to stand in.
How to do it

items: Right-click the destination block with a bound gem to record it. You land on top of it, or on the ground beneath if you clicked grass or a thin layer of snow. For a machine, a chest or anything else that opens, sneak + right-click.

Right-click the teleporter. The gem linked to an MRU source goes in the left slot, and the destination gem in the right slot. Hover over the status bar in its screen to see what the trip costs and whether the destination is safe.
Stand on top of the teleporter and stay put. The status changes from "Ready" to "Charging", and after {cfg:machines.magical_teleporter.ticks_required|sec} you are sent.
If you land on another teleporter, step off and back on before it will charge again. The same goes after a failed trip.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: A firework bang, and you are standing on top of that block, with the trip's MRU taken from the teleporter.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: When the charge is full, the destination is checked. It needs something to stand on, two free blocks of room, nothing harmful such as lava, fire, cactus or powder snow, and it has to be a place where you may change blocks. The Nether's bedrock roof can't be reached. If the check fails you stay put, no MRU is spent and the screen says why, so step off, fix it and step back on.

blocks.title: Getting back
blocks.text: One teleporter only goes one way. For a round trip, build one at each end and sneak + right-click the other teleporter with a gem to make it the destination. After arriving, step off and back on to return. Each one needs its own Matter of Eternity, so count your Nether Stars first.
Cost
Same world: {cfg:machines.magical_teleporter.mru_usage} × (east-west + up-down + north-south distance) ÷ 3 MRU, at most {cfg:machines.magical_teleporter.max_mru}

For example, 60 blocks east and 30 north add up to 90, which costs {cfg:machines.magical_teleporter.mru_usage|mul:30} MRU per trip. Distance is measured from the teleporter to the block the gem points at.

cells: only with a full tank; takes all {cfg:machines.magical_teleporter.max_mru} MRU

blocks.text: Fine print

items: If there isn't enough MRU for the trip, the charge pauses and carries on once MRU is back. A different person, a removed gem or a broken structure starts it over.
A redstone signal pauses the charge.
You can't be sent while riding something or carrying a passenger, so get off first.
A teleporter inside someone else's claim only charges for players who have permission there.
While charging it loads the area around the destination. If that still isn't ready when the charge is full, it waits a few more seconds and then counts the trip as failed.

items.text: Every trip leaks 0–{cfg:machines.magical_teleporter.max_corruption_gen} MRU around it (see [[crafting/corruption]]).

blocks.text: Further reading: binding and unbinding gems in [[crafting/bound_gem]]; a strong source to power it is the [[void_machines/ultra_heat_generator]].
The original research book called it a "warp gate" and used a whole row of exclamation marks to stress that it reaches other dimensions.

entries.title: Magical Building Wand
entries.summary: Fill, clear or swap a whole area at once
items: essentialcraft5:magical_builder_fill
essentialcraft5:magical_builder_clear
essentialcraft5:magical_builder_clear_matching
essentialcraft5:magical_builder_clear_others
essentialcraft5:magical_builder_replace_all

blocks.text: Goal (optional): craft a Magical Building Wand and fill an area, clear it or swap every block in it for another in one go. It is the second tier of the building wand: compared with the [[gear/paving_wand|Paving Wand]] it adds four modes that remove or replace blocks, two more shapes, Wall and Surface, and handles far more blocks per job. It runs on MRU and puts whatever it breaks straight into your inventory.
Prepare

{item:essentialcraft5:world_interactor} ×2, {item:essentialcraft5:void_plating} ×2, {item:essentialcraft5:void_core} ×1, {item:essentialcraft5:whitelist_filter} ×2, {item:essentialcraft5:magical_digger} ×1 and {item:essentialcraft5:magic_plate} ×1, where pale, mithriline or demonic plates also work for the last one. It comes out in Fill mode with the Two Points shape.

The World Interacting Device is made on an ordinary crafting table ([[crafting/magician_crafts]]). Void Plates are covered in [[hoanna/void_plating]] and cores in [[hoanna/relics]], filters in [[logistics/filters]] and the digger in [[gear/magical_digger]].

If you already have a Paving Wand, put it in place of either whitelist filter in the recipe to upgrade it straight into a Magical Building Wand. Stored MRU, the selected block and fitted modules are kept.

blocks.caption: Either the upper or the lower filter can be replaced

blocks.text: How to do it

items: Holding the wand, right-click one block to set the first corner and another to set the second. The box between them is the selection, outlined in magenta while the wand is in your main hand.
Sneak + right-click a block to <hl>select</hl> it. Fill and Replace All place that block, and Remove Selected and Remove All But Selected compare against it.

For the modes that place blocks, Fill and Replace All, carry the selected block's item, then right-click the air to start. The wand works through the area block by block, so keep holding it and stay close while it works.

Sneak + right-click the air to stop. If nothing is running, this clears both corners instead, while the selected block stays. Once both corners are set, this is also how you clear them to start a new selection.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: With the wand in your main hand you see a magenta selection box; right-clicking the air starts the work, and when it finishes you are told how many blocks were changed.
The Plane and Line shapes, the wand key, the Blueprint Table, where materials come from and how undo works are all the same as for the Paving Wand; see [[gear/paving_wand]].
The three tiers

The building wand comes in three tiers: tier 1 is the [[gear/paving_wand|Paving Wand]], tier 2 is this one, and tier 3 is the [[void_machines/ascended_builder|Ascended Magical Building Wand]], made from this one on a Magician Table.
Fitted modules change these limits further; see [[void_machines/builder_module]].
Five modes

rows: Places the selected block into empty air only
Breaks every block in the area; no selected block needed
Breaks only blocks of the selected kind
Breaks everything except the selected kind
Places the selected block into air, water and lava, swaps every other block for it, leaves ones that already match

blocks.text: The MRU in this table is the tier 2 price; for tier 3, see the previous section.

blocks.title: Switching modes
blocks.text: Put the wand alone in a crafting grid to switch to the next mode: Fill → Remove All → Remove Selected → Remove All But Selected → Replace All → Fill. You can also pick a mode directly on the Area page of the Blueprint Table. Stored MRU, both corners, the selected block and fitted modules are kept.
Wall

From tier 2 on there are two more shapes, <hl>Wall</hl> and <hl>Surface</hl>. Both are picked on the Area page of the Blueprint Table, and a single right-click starts the work. In Fill mode a Wall rises from the block just outside the face you click, centred on the crosshair and spreading to your left and right. When removing or replacing it starts from the clicked block itself; see "Range when removing or replacing" below.

items: Default size is <t>5</t> wide and <t>4</t> high. Hold the wand key and scroll to change the width; add sneak to change the height. With an even width the extra block goes to your right.
Click the bottom face of a block and the wall starts from the block below it and grows downwards, so it can hang from a ceiling.
Right-click the air and the wall stands one block in front of you, rising from the layer at your feet.
Width and height are each at most the side limit, and width times height at most the largest job; if it is too big, the height is cut first.

blocks.text: Surface

Surface takes the face you click and follows the connected blocks of the same kind, covering the whole layer outside that face. It is handy for putting a layer over uneven ground or facing a whole wall. The area is decided by the connected blocks, so there is no size to adjust.

items: Blocks count as connected when they are the same kind, the face pointing the same way is exposed, and what lies outside it is air, grass, water or something else that can be replaced. A step of one block up or down still connects; two or more does not.

Measured from where you clicked, the whole patch fits inside the side limit each way and holds at most the largest job; anything beyond that is cut off, keeping the part nearest to where you clicked, and the start message says so.

After the right-click the wand first spends a few ticks <hl>measuring</hl> the connected patch, then starts; meanwhile the line below the crosshair says it is measuring. Right-clicking again during that time does not start a second job, and sneak + right-click the air cancels.
If the face you clicked is covered by another block, there is nothing to follow and you are told so.

blocks.text: Aiming range

Plane, Wall and Surface can be aimed at any block within work range. With the crosshair on a distant block, the area there is marked out as usual, and a right-click starts the work there. The work range of each tier is listed in the tier table above.

items: Two Points and Line cannot aim at long range; they still use the normal interaction distance.
The face you click in the distance must be clearly visible. If something is in the way, or it is too far to pin down, you are told the face can't be made out; try again from another angle.
The whole area must still be within work range, and its chunks must be loaded.

blocks.text: Range when removing or replacing

Remove All, Remove Selected, Remove All But Selected and Replace All act on blocks that are already there, so in these modes a Plane, Line or Wall starts from the clicked block itself, not the block outside it.

items: Plane: click a top or bottom face and the layer the clicked block sits in is worked on, centred on that block. Click a side face and the layer runs from the clicked block into the blocks behind it.

Wall: click a top or side face and it rises from the clicked block; click a bottom face and it hangs down from the clicked block. On a side face the wall spreads along the clicked face, so that wall itself is worked on.
Line: starts from the clicked block and still runs in the direction you face.
Right-clicking the air starts from the same place as in Fill mode.

blocks.text: In these modes a Surface acts on the connected layer of blocks itself, so you can strip or swap a whole patch of ground or a wall's facing. Fill is unaffected and still lays its layer outside.
Undo

items: Hold the wand key and right-click, or click Undo last on the Blueprint Table, to undo the last placement; the rules are in [[gear/paving_wand]]. Tier 2 can only undo the most recent one; tier 3 can undo the last 3, one after another.
Blocks broken by the removing modes cannot be put back. With Replace All only the placed blocks are undone, and the blocks that were swapped out do not come back.

If the last job was a removal, finished or not, neither the wand key with right-click nor Undo last reaches back to an earlier placement; you are told that the last job was a removal, which cannot be undone. A placement made after the removal can be undone as usual.

blocks.text: Where the MRU comes from

The wand holds 5,000 MRU of its own and comes out empty, so charge it in the [[storage/charging_chamber]]. It draws from the storage items you carry first ([[storage/soul_storage]]) and only then from itself.

The wand's own 5,000 MRU only breaks 20 blocks, so for big jobs carry soul storage items. One {item:essentialcraft5:matter_of_eternity} holds a million. You only pay for blocks it actually changes, and air and skipped blocks cost nothing.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: Blocks in someone else's claim are left alone and cost nothing, but once {cfg:general.builder.denied_limit} have been refused the wand stops. After the first refusal it asks before placing each block instead of bumping into every one, so keep your selection out of other people's claims. When the whole job is done, the message says how many blocks were left unchanged for lack of permission. Bedrock, barriers and blocks such as chests, furnaces, signs and machines are skipped in every mode, and water and lava are skipped when removing.

Some claims allow breaking but not placing, so the check passes and the actual placement is refused. The wand also stops after {cfg:general.builder.denied_streak_limit} actual placements or removals in a row are refused; any block changed in between resets the count. With Replace All, blocks in such claims are removed but cannot be replaced; the end message reports how many on a separate line.
Fine print

items: Broken blocks go into your inventory, and what doesn't fit drops at your feet; with a Salvage Module fitted they go into carried containers first, see [[void_machines/builder_module]]. Drops follow each block's own loot table, as if mined with the right tool but no enchantments. Stone gives cobblestone, diamond ore gives one diamond, and glass, ice and other blocks that need Silk Touch give nothing.
Doors, tall flowers and extended pistons come off whole. Removing works from the top layer down, so sand and gravel don't fall.

Doors, beds, tall flowers and blocks such as chests, signs, campfires and machines can't be selected. If Replace All may break a block but not place one there, the spot is left as air and is charged as a removal.
With a block in your off hand, Fill and Replace All place that block instead of the selected one.

How placed blocks face, spots where a block can't stay, falling blocks, queueing and Creative mode work the same as for the Paving Wand; see [[gear/paving_wand]]. In Creative mode, broken blocks give nothing back either.

blocks.text: Further reading: tier 3 in [[void_machines/ascended_builder]], modules in [[void_machines/builder_module]]; for plain mining without a selection, the [[gear/magical_digger]] is handier.

The original research book subtitled it with a single line of code, world.edit();. Its first page said the wand can do almost anything, then reminded you that with great power comes great responsibility.

entries.title: Ascended Magical Building Wand
entries.summary: Ascend it on a Magician Table: bigger jobs, less MRU

blocks.text: Goal (optional): ascend a Magical Building Wand to tier 3 on a Magician Table. Afterwards one job can cover {cfg:general.builder.ascended.max_volume} blocks instead of {cfg:general.builder.max_volume}, work range and speed both go up, each block costs {cfg:general.builder.ascended.cost_multiplier|pct} of the usual MRU, and there is one more module slot.
Prepare

Put a Magical Building Wand in the centre of a Magician Table, in any mode, and around it {item:essentialcraft5:demonic_core} ×2, {item:essentialcraft5:void_mru_reactor} ×1 and {item:essentialcraft5:ackronite_ingot} ×1. The craft takes 100,000 MRU.
The Magician Table is covered in [[crafting/magician_table]], demonic cores and ackronite in [[demons/ackronite]], and the MRU reactor in [[hoanna/relics]].
How to do it

items: Put the Magical Building Wand in the centre slot of the Magician Table and lay out the other ingredients around it as the recipe shows.
Supply the Magician Table with MRU; when the progress bar fills you get the ascended wand.
The wand keeps its mode, stored MRU, both corners, selected block, shape and fitted modules, and its own MRU capacity goes from 5,000 to 20,000.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: You have the ascended wand in your inventory. Its name becomes Ascended Magical Building Wand, it gets a new look, and its tooltip says Tier 3.
What changes

items.text: Undoing in turn: hold the wand key and right-click once to undo the latest placement; do it again to undo the one before that, up to 3 back. Each one must be undone within {cfg:general.builder.undo_window_seconds} seconds of being placed. If a removal was done in between, only the placements made after it can be undone.

items: The ascended wand can still switch modes in a crafting grid, and stays tier 3 afterwards.
An ascended wand cannot be ascended again; put in the centre slot of a Magician Table, it does not start.

blocks.text: Further reading: what to put in the extra module slot is covered in [[void_machines/builder_module]].

entries.title: Building Wand Modules
entries.summary: Range, Haste, Efficiency, Reach, Mixing, Salvage
items: essentialcraft5:builder_module_range
essentialcraft5:builder_module_haste
essentialcraft5:builder_module_efficiency
essentialcraft5:builder_module_reach
essentialcraft5:builder_module_mix
essentialcraft5:builder_module_salvage

blocks.text: Goal (optional): craft a wand module and fit it to a Magical Building Wand or Paving Wand. Modules let the wand cover more blocks per job, work faster, use less MRU or reach farther, lay several kinds of blocks mixed together, or put what it breaks straight into carried containers.
Prepare
All six modules are made on an ordinary crafting table, with no fixed pattern.

items: essentialcraft5:builder_module_range
essentialcraft5:builder_module_haste
essentialcraft5:builder_module_efficiency
essentialcraft5:builder_module_reach
essentialcraft5:builder_module_mix
essentialcraft5:builder_module_salvage
{item:essentialcraft5:pale_plate}: see [[alloys/pale]]; {item:essentialcraft5:elemental_core}: see [[elements/parts]].
{item:essentialcraft5:magic_purified_redstone_alloy}: see [[alloys/purified_alloys]]; {item:essentialcraft5:air_focus}: see [[essence/fuel_and_focus]].
{item:essentialcraft5:mru_resonating_crystal}: see [[alloys/resonating_crystal]]; {item:essentialcraft5:soul_shard}: see [[storage/soul_storage]].
{item:essentialcraft5:eye_of_absorption}: see [[crafting/radiating_chamber]]; {item:essentialcraft5:world_interactor}: see [[crafting/magician_crafts]].

{item:essentialcraft5:crystal_dust}: see [[alloys/crystal_dust]]; {item:essentialcraft5:whitelist_filter}: see [[logistics/filters]]; {item:essentialcraft5:magical_chest}: see [[logistics/magical_chest]].

blocks.text: Fitting and removing

items: Put one wand and one module in a crafting grid with nothing else; the result is the wand with that module fitted. One module goes in at a time, and stored MRU and settings are kept.
The Paving Wand has 2 module slots, the Magical Building Wand 3 and the Ascended Magical Building Wand 4. Each kind of module fits only once, and nothing more fits once the slots are full.

Modules are removed on the Modules page of the Blueprint Table: click the × next to a module and it goes back to your inventory, or drops at your feet if your inventory is full. The same page can also switch a single module off; a switched-off module still takes up its slot.
Modules cannot be fitted or removed while a job is running, paused or queued.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: You have any one module in your inventory. Once one is fitted, the wand's tooltip gains a Modules line listing what is fitted and how many slots are used.
Fitted modules stay on the wand when it is upgraded to the next tier or switched to another mode, and an upgrade never has fewer slots.
Six modules

rows: Work range +{cfg:general.builder.modules.reach.reach_bonus} blocks; Plane, Wall and Surface can be aimed as far as the work range
Lays up to {cfg:general.builder.modules.mix.max_kinds} kinds of blocks mixed in set proportions
Broken blocks go into carried containers first; a discard list can be set

blocks.text: Range, Haste, Efficiency

items: Range raises the blocks per job and the side length, rounded down; how far apart the two corners of Two Points can be does not change. Whatever is fitted, one job never goes over {cfg:general.builder.hard_max_volume} blocks.
Haste lets this wand do more per tick, but when many players are building at once they share the total per tick, so the real speed may not reach the full multiple.
Efficiency discounts the wand's own price, rounded down. For an ascended wand the ascended price is taken first, then the Efficiency multiplier.
The actual limits with modules fitted are shown in the wand's tooltip and on the Modules page of the Blueprint Table.

blocks.text: Reach

Reach adds {cfg:general.builder.modules.reach.reach_bonus} blocks to the work range, so the job keeps going even if you walk a little farther away. Plane, Wall and Surface can be aimed as far as the work range, so they reach farther as well.
Mixing

With a Mixing Module, Fill and Replace All can lay several kinds of blocks mixed in set proportions, for patterned floors or weathered-looking walls. The proportions are kept in the wand's <hl>mix table</hl>.

items: Open the Blueprint Table and go to the Blocks page; the mix table is on the right.
Click Add one, then click a block in the list on the left to add it to the table, starting at weight 1. Up to {cfg:general.builder.modules.mix.max_kinds} kinds.

Each block's weight is a whole number from 1 to 9, set with the − and + buttons beside it. The higher the weight, the more of it is laid, and its percentage is shown next to it. Click × to take a kind out.
While the table has blocks in it, the wand lays from the table and ignores the selected block and the block in your off hand; with an empty table it lays the selected block as usual.

Which kind goes in each spot is worked out from its position, so the pattern drawn on the blueprint is what you get. The same table gives a different pattern in a different place, and setting the table again changes the pattern too.
When one kind runs out, the other kinds in the table fill in; the job only pauses when they have all run out.
If you don't carry everything needed, the wand lists how much of each kind you carry and how much is needed before starting; click again to start anyway.
With Replace All, every kind in the table counts as the selected block, and spots that already hold one of them are left alone. The removing modes don't mix.
On undo, each spot refunds the kind that was actually laid there.

blocks.text: Salvage

With a Salvage Module, whatever the removing modes and Replace All break goes into the containers you carry first, then your inventory, and drops at your feet if both are full. The Salvage Module only fits tier 2 and above.

items: Open the Blueprint Table and go to the Modules page; the <hl>discard list</hl> is on the right.

The candidates list items already on the list first, then items you have recently broken, then blocks you carry. Click one to add it to the list; red-framed items are on the list, and clicking again takes them off.
Items on the list are thrown away as they are broken, going neither into containers nor your inventory. The list holds up to {cfg:general.builder.modules.salvage.discard_max} kinds.
Containers are filled in the same order materials are taken from them: bag-like items in your inventory, off hand, armor and accessory slots, outermost layer only.
While another container screen is open, broken items skip carried containers and go straight to your inventory.

items.text: The discard list matches by item type, ignoring enchantments and names.

items: Materials refunded by undo skip Salvage and go straight to your inventory.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: Anything on the discard list is gone as soon as it is broken and cannot be recovered. Check the list before breaking anything rare.

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:ember_forge}
items: essentialcraft5:ember_forge
entries.summary: Forge embers and focuses into a sword

blocks.text: Goal (optional): build an Ember Forge and forge 4 embers and 4 elemental focuses into an {item:essentialcraft5:forged_elemental_sword}. The forge itself needs no MRU. Embers are what is left of the fire that burned Hoanna.
Prepare

items: The forge itself takes a {item:essentialcraft5:magical_screen}, an {item:essentialcraft5:void_mru_reactor}, an {item:essentialcraft5:magic_purified_ender_scale_alloy}, 2 {item:essentialcraft5:magic_fortified_plating}s, a {item:essentialcraft5:void_core}, 2 {item:essentialcraft5:void_plating}s and 1 {item:essentialcraft5:matter_of_eternity}. The recipe is below.
29 {item:essentialcraft5:void_stone} ([[hoanna/void_stone]]), plus 4 {item:essentialcraft5:pale_plating} and 4 {item:essentialcraft5:magic_plating} ([[alloys/plating]]), all in any colors.
Each sword takes 4 embers and 4 elemental focuses. Embers are common in the chests of Hoanna's ruins, about nine per chest on average ([[hoanna/relics]]).

The focuses are the hard part. Each sword uses up 4 whole, and you build them up slowly by extracting essences from crystals ([[essence/fuel_and_focus]]). Decide which element you want before you start, since [[void_machines/ember_sword]] lists what each one does. The main line's [[demons/demonic_pentacle]] also needs 4 {item:essentialcraft5:fire_focus}, so set those aside first.

blocks.text: Layout
Lay a 5×5 floor of Void Stone and put the forge on the middle block. On the forge's layer, place a Void Stone in each corner and a Pale Plating two blocks out on each side.
One layer up, place a Magic Plating in each corner, right on top of those four Void Stones.
How to do it

items: Throw one ember onto each of the four Pale Platings and one focus onto each of the four Magic Platings. Whatever lands there is straightened and held in place, and passers-by and mobs can't pick it up.

items.text: Wait for night. {cfg:machines.ember_forge.ticks_required|sec} after all eight are in place, a sword pops out of the top of the forge.
{cfg:machines.ember_forge.ticks_required|sec} after all eight are in place, a sword pops out of the top of the forge.

items: If you can't tell what it's waiting for, right-click the forge with an empty hand. It tells you which spot is missing, how many items are left, whether it's waiting for night, or how far along it is.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: Once the structure is right, spell particles drift around the forge, a trail of red sparks links each ember to it, and each focus glows with a blue spark while purple particles stream into the forge. A while into forging, lava sparks rise from the top and a portal sound plays every two or three seconds.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: The finished sword lands on top of the forge, and at night mobs that pick up items will grab it. Light the area up and stay close until it's done.
Fine print

items: Each forging takes only one item per spot. A whole stack of embers on one plating is used one at a time, and the rest goes into later swords. Focuses are used up whole whatever their durability.

items.text: It only works at night. During the day nothing happens even with all eight in place, and if dawn breaks halfway, the progress starts over the next night. Places without a sky, like the Nether and the End, work at any time, and a thunderstorm counts as night too.

items: A redstone signal pauses it and keeps the progress. If an item goes missing or the structure loses a block, progress starts over.
Sneak + right-click with an empty hand to release everything it is holding. It won't hold anything again for 10 seconds, so that is how you take back items you put in the wrong place.

blocks.text: The original research book's subtitle for it is a single line, "So shiny... So warm..."

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:forged_elemental_sword}
items: essentialcraft5:forged_elemental_sword
entries.summary: Focuses set the element, ember pairs add the rest

blocks.text: Goal (optional): forge an Ember Elemental Sword in the [[void_machines/ember_forge]]. Its damage and special effects depend entirely on the focuses and embers you put in.
The four focuses set a <hl>primary</hl> and a <hl>secondary element</hl>, and the four embers pair up to add extra damage and on-hit effects. The three tables below cover each in turn.

blocks.title: Plan your sword
blocks.text: Four focuses of one kind make that element both primary and secondary. Three of one kind plus another fix the primary, and the secondary is picked at random between the two. Four different embers give the most pairs.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: The sword's tooltip lists its primary and secondary elements, the ember bonus and every effect it can trigger.
Primary element

Among the four focuses, an element that appears more often than each of the other three is the primary element. Ties, and one of each, give "Combined". The primary element sets the base damage and an on-hit effect that costs <t>50</t> MRU per hit.

rows: Sets the target on fire for 5 s
Weakness and Slowness on the target for 2 s
Blindness and Mining Fatigue on the target for 2 s
Speed and Strength for you for 2.5 s

blocks.text: The bonus works like a vanilla sword's, so the attack damage in the tooltip includes the 1 point of your bare hand. For comparison, a netherite sword is +7.
Secondary element

The secondary element is picked at random from the elements among the focuses. It triggers when you press right-click and costs <t>50</t> MRU, and at the same time the sword comes up to block like a shield.

rows: Fire Resistance for 2.5 s; hostile mobs within 2 blocks catch fire for 2 s (villagers, pets and other players don't)
Regeneration for 2.5 s; does nothing and costs nothing while you already have Regeneration

blocks.text: Ember pairs

items: essentialcraft5:acidic_ember
essentialcraft5:chaos_ember
essentialcraft5:common_ember
essentialcraft5:corrupted_ember
essentialcraft5:crystal_ember
essentialcraft5:divine_ember
essentialcraft5:magical_ember
essentialcraft5:flame_ember

blocks.text: The 4 embers pair up by kind. Four of the same kind make no pairs, and four different kinds make 6. Look each pair up below. Damage bonuses add up pair by pair, to at most {cfg:general.ember_sword.max_ember_damage|sign} in total, and an effect given by several pairs only counts once.
If there are on-hit effects, each hit costs another <t>50</t> MRU and the effects last 3 s. Damage bonuses alone cost nothing.

rows: Hurts the wielder, Hunger II on the target
Dispel (strips one beneficial effect from the target)

items: Lightning: a bolt comes down on the target you hit, dealing 5 damage and setting it on fire for 8 s, and you get Fire Resistance II for 3 s. It only strikes that one target, doesn't set blocks alight and doesn't turn villagers or pigs into anything else. It strikes at most once every 2 seconds.
Hurts the wielder: you take 2 damage on every hit.

Dispel: strips one beneficial status effect from the target, endless ones first and otherwise the one with the most time left. Harmful effects are never touched. Corrosion: the target can't heal for 3 s, and natural regeneration, Regeneration and Instant Health all do nothing.

items.text: The four highest-damage embers are Acidic, Chaotic, Smouldering and Burning. Their 6 pairs add up to +36, at the price of hurting yourself.

Acidic, Chaotic, Smouldering and Burning make 6 pairs adding up to +36, but the ember bonus only counts up to {cfg:general.ember_sword.max_ember_damage|sign}. Reaching that is enough, so there's no need to force this combination and its self-damage.

items: To avoid both the self-damage and the extra MRU per hit, use Acidic, Smouldering and Burning, with the fourth repeating any of them. Their 3 pairs add up to +21 with no on-hit effects at all.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: When the MRU runs out every effect stops, the self-damage included, and only the attack damage is left. If you use it a lot, carry a soul storage item, since the sword draws from that first.
The pairs with on-hit effects can also be made into ember inlays and set into other weapons ([[void_machines/ember_inlay]]).

Fighting with it builds attunement points, up to stage 2: each stage raises its attack damage by {cfg:general.gear_growth.ember_sword.attack_per_stage|pct} of the original, stage 1 adds lifesteal, and stage 2 awakens <hl>Element Burst</hl>, a chance to blast the primary element around the target. A stage 2 sword can also be reforged into a {item:essentialcraft5:verdict_blade} ([[attunement/ember_sword]]).
Fine print

items: It never loses durability, even when mining or blocking, and it can be enchanted.

It holds 5,000 MRU and charges in the [[storage/charging_chamber]]. Costs come first from storage items you carry, such as a {item:essentialcraft5:soul_shard} ([[storage/soul_storage]]), and then from the sword itself.
Blocking works like a shield, so an axe hit can knock it down for 5 seconds.
Forging the same materials twice can give a different secondary element.
The creative inventory has two Ember Elemental Swords, one empty and one full of MRU. Neither has been forged, so they have no primary or secondary element and no ember bonus.

blocks.text: In the original mod this table of pairs sat in the code and almost never took effect. Here it finally does.

entries.title: {item:essentialcraft5:ember_inlay}
items: essentialcraft5:ember_inlay
entries.summary: Put a pair of embers' effects into any weapon

blocks.text: Goal (optional): make an ember inlay and set it into a weapon on an anvil. From then on, every hit that lands with that weapon triggers the pair's on-hit effect from the [[void_machines/ember_sword]]. Swords, axes and bows from other mods work too.

Craft two different embers, a {item:essentialcraft5:pale_gem} and a {item:essentialcraft5:combined_magical_alloys} together in any arrangement to get one inlay that remembers the pair. Only the 14 pairs with an on-hit effect can be made. The damage-only pairs can't, and neither can Chaotic + Smouldering, which adds damage along with backlash.
Inlaying

items: Put the weapon in the left slot of an {item:minecraft:anvil} and the inlay in the right one.
Take out the inlaid weapon. It costs {cfg:general.ember_inlay.anvil_levels} levels and 1 inlay, and the weapon's tooltip gains an "Ember Inlay: …" line.
A weapon holds one inlay. Inlaying another pair replaces it, and the old inlay is not returned.

blocks.title: Done when
blocks.text: You take your first inlaid weapon out of an anvil.
Which weapons

items: Swords, axes, pickaxes, shovels, hoes and tridents, plus similar items from other mods, and shields and fishing rods too, all of which trigger when you land a hit holding them in your main hand;
bows and crossbows;
not the {item:essentialcraft5:forged_elemental_sword}, which already carries embers;
one at a time; stacked items can't be inlaid.

blocks.text: When a hit lands

Land a melee hit with the inlaid weapon, or land an arrow while holding the inlaid bow or crossbow in your main hand, and {cfg:general.ember_inlay.mru_per_hit} MRU is spent to trigger the pair's effect. The MRU comes from storage items you carry first. If you can't pay, nothing happens.

The effect is exactly that pair's effect on the Ember Elemental Sword and lasts 3 seconds ([[void_machines/ember_sword]] has the table). Lightning still strikes at most once every 2 seconds, and backlash still hurts you. Inlays give effects only, no extra damage, so an inlaid sword hits as hard as before.

blocks.title: Pitfall
blocks.text: A hit doesn't land if a claim, a team or the rule against players hurting each other stops it, if something else cancels the damage, or if it does no damage because the target is briefly invulnerable. Then no MRU is spent and nothing triggers. Thorns, spell damage, damage dealt by baubles such as the {item:essentialcraft5:nu_amulet}'s chain, and the ring of spikes from a fully raised {item:essentialcraft5:spiky_shield} don't count as weapon hits.
Fine print

items: A sweep counts once for every creature it hits, and charges MRU for each.
Several pieces of damage dealt to the same creature at the same instant, such as the extra hit some other mods' weapons add to an attack, count as one hit and are charged once.
A hit that the target's absorption soaks up entirely, such as the golden hearts from a golden apple, still lands. It triggers and costs MRU as usual.
Bows and crossbows go by what is in your main hand when the arrow hits, so if you switch to something else, that arrow won't trigger.
Mining and blocking cost no MRU; only hits that land on a creature do.
All 14 inlays show up in the recipe book, and an inlay's tooltip says which pair it holds and what it triggers.

blocks.text: In the original mod, embers could only go into the Ember Elemental Sword. Inlays came later.
